Apple Maps listing setup

Apple Maps listing setup via Apple Business Connect

Setting up and verifying your business on Apple Business Connect so iPhone users find you, for businesses in Denton and DFW.

What this is

Apple Maps is the default map on every iPhone, and iPhones are roughly half the phones in the United States. If someone asks Siri for a business near them, or searches Spotlight, or taps a map link, they are in Apple's data rather than Google's.

Most local businesses have never claimed their Apple listing, and many do not know one exists.

What you get

What setup involves

  • 01

    Claiming through Apple Business Connect

    Apple's own free tool for managing how your business appears. Your business may already be listed from third-party data without anyone from the business ever touching it.

  • 02

    Three surfaces at once

    Apple Maps, Siri and Spotlight all draw on the same record. Claiming it once fixes your details across all three.

  • 03

    Categories, hours and contact details

    Set properly, including holiday hours, which Apple surfaces prominently on the day.

  • 04

    Photographs and a showcase

    Apple lets you add images and promotional cards that appear on the place card, which is a level of presentation most businesses never use.

  • 05

    Verification

    Apple verifies ownership before handing over control. The process is generally straightforward and slower than Bing.

What it costs

Quoted after a free consult, because what it takes depends entirely on what you already have. Book a call, I will tell you what is involved, and you get a number before anything starts. If you are already on a plan, this may fold into it: the tiers are on the pricing page.

A small one-time job, commonly bundled with Bing Places setup.

How this differs

Different platform, different tool, different reason. Apple matters because of iPhone share and the three places Apple surfaces a business: Maps, Siri and Spotlight. Bing Places matters because of Windows and the assistants that pull from Bing.

Neither replaces your Google Business Profile, and if only one is getting attention it should be Google.

Like Bing, this is a one-time job with a modest and real payoff. Worth doing, not worth a retainer.

Questions

What people ask

Am I already on Apple Maps?

Quite possibly, assembled from third-party data. Search for yourself in Maps on an iPhone. If you are there with details nobody at your business chose, that is exactly the situation claiming it fixes.

Does this affect Google rankings?

No. They are separate systems. The benefit is being correct and present for iPhone users, which is a different audience rather than a boost to the same one.

Does Siri use this?

Yes. Siri and Spotlight both draw on the same business data, so claiming the listing affects all three surfaces at once.

Is there a monthly cost?

Apple Business Connect is free. The only cost is setting it up properly, and it does not need ongoing management beyond updating details when they change.
